facts.statement: Papiliovenator uniquely possessed a short, subtriangular snout similar to Early Cretaceous troodontids like Mei long, differing from the long snouts of Late Cretaceous relatives.
facts.quote: Uniquely, its snout was short and subtriangular, more similar to that of Early Cretaceous troodontids such as Mei long than the long, low snouts of Late Cretaceous troodontids.

facts.statement: Fossils of Papiliovenator were found in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: from the Bayan Mandahu Formation of Inner Mongolia, China

facts.statement: The remains of this dinosaur were discovered in the Bayan Mandahu Formation in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Sus restos se enontrarón en la Formación Bayan Mandahu en Mongolia Interior, China.

facts.statement: Papiliovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 83 and 72 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, aproximadamente entre 83 a 72 millones de años durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: The time range for Papiliovenator is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Papiliovenator neimengguensis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Papiliovenator neimengguensis.

facts.statement: Papiliovenator is classified within the family Troodontidae.
Researchers classify Papiliovenator as the earliest-diverging member of a clade containing all Late Cretaceous troodontids, excluding Almas ukhaa.
facts.quote: Pei et al. recover Papiliovenator as the earliest-diverging member of a clade consisting of all Late Cretaceous troodontids except for Almas ukhaa.

facts.statement: Unique skeletal traits of Papiliovenator suggest a high diversity of troodontid body forms in the Late Cretaceous Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: This and other unique traits of its skeleton suggest a high diversity of troodontid morphotypes in the Late Cretaceous Gobi Desert.
